target_customer: Home buyers and sellers in Argentina and Mexico, and partner real estate agents who pay commission on closed deals
problem: Buying and selling homes in Latin America is opaque and slow. Mudafy offers a tech enabled broker with virtual tours, benchmark pricing and agent tools.
business_model: commission on successful real estate transactions
product_category: tech enabled real estate brokerage and agent network

founders.name: Franco Forte
founders.background_notes: Forbes Argentina (Nov 2021) says both founders studied Industrial Engineering at ITBA; it does not say who studied what, but names both.

founders.name: Luqui Diaz
founders.background_notes: Forbes Argentina calls him Lucas Diaz; YC page lists Luqui Diaz.

technical_complexity.rationale: A listings site, virtual tours and booking tools are standard web work; difficulty is operational across brokers and local markets.

defensibility.rationale: Agent network and listing data help, but brokerage services and portals are easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Regional digital brokers Loft and QuintoAndar had layoffs in 2022 per TechCrunch; Mudafy cut 70 percent of corporate staff in January 2023.

market_need_then: Forbes Argentina (2021) reports Mudafy sold properties worth over 100M USD in 2021 with 20 percent monthly growth, suggesting demand for a digital brokerage.

branding.domain_note: Operates mudafy.com.ar and mudafy.com.mx country domains.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: A new way to find your property (Spanish)

rebrands.why: Forbes Argentina says 2019 was when they started the project and took the current name; the earlier name is not given

brand_strength.rationale: Regional press coverage exists but nothing on brand assets or community.

outcome_analysis: Mudafy joined YC in 2019, raised a 1.6M seed, expanded to Mexico in 2020 and closed a 10M Series A in August 2022. In January 2023 it cut 70 percent of corporate staff, with the CEO citing higher rates and reduced investment, but it continues to operate and launched an AI real estate network in 2025.
notes: Competitors left empty: Forbes Argentina (Nov 2021) lists Redfin, Compass, Opendoor, Housfy and Purplebricks as reference models, not competitors, and the TechCrunch 2022 rivals Loft and QuintoAndar are too late. Total raised about 13M per TechCrunch, so about 3M came before the Series A; the 1.6M seed from 37 investors is from Forbes Argentina only. Aggregators mention a 2023 0.2M round (unverified). Founding year conflicts 2018 vs 2019.
